title: GPT-6 Sol vs Claude Opus 5.5 Price Cut: How Much Will Your AI Bill Drop?
description:
GPT-6 Sol's price list shows eight prices for one model. This video reads it cell by cell, then estimates the monthly token cost of five models, including GPT-6 Sol, Luna and Opus 5.5, for three sample usage levels.
For anyone who uses an AI API or subscription and wants to know whether "50% cheaper" or "40% less" actually has anything to do with their own bill.

The video starts with the eight cells of GPT-6 Sol's standard price: input, cache read, cache write and output, each with a short-context and a long-context price. Then it covers batch, fast mode and promo pricing, works out the monthly cost of three sample usages (chat, agent, bulk processing), and finally unpacks what Anthropic's 40%, 20% and 60% are each measured against.

Amounts are illustrative token costs for short context and standard processing; they do not include cache write, storage, tool or other service fees, and the bulk processing column does not use the batch discount. Prices change; check the official site on the day.

Further reading: API price comparison: cost per million tokens by vendor (official price lists, mid-September)

c32b.text: So a cache write costs more than input.

66qr.text: Caching doesn't always work. Ten questions on one file don't guarantee ten hits.

4b3g.text: The start must match; one changed word breaks the rest.

medc.text: It also needs length: at least 1,024 tokens.

xrwh.text: Left too long, it expires and must be redone.

9wrt.text: But switching means retesting quality, and time is a cost.

5snu.text: Switching? Two steps first, not by feel.

gkup.text: First, open your usage page and see what each token type costs.

m7k4.text: Back to the start: which price will you pay?
